title: Jan Dhan Yojana Turns 12 With 59 Crore Accounts and Rs 3.17 Lakh Crore in Deposits
excerpt: The world's largest financial inclusion scheme has brought 89% of Indian adults into the banking system, with 56% of accounts held by women
body:
• More than 59 crore bank accounts have been opened under PMJDY since its 2014 launch, with total deposits reaching Rs 3.17 lakh crore as of August 19, 2026.
  • Women hold 56% of all Jan Dhan accounts, and 78% of accounts are in rural and semi-urban areas, making it a cornerstone of India's push toward financial gender parity.
  • India's bank account ownership has risen from 35.2% in 2011 to 89% in 2024 according to the World Bank, with the scheme enabling Rs 53 lakh crore in direct benefit transfers through the JAM trinity.

The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, the world's largest financial inclusion initiative, completed 12 years on Thursday with more than 59 crore bank accounts opened and total deposits crossing Rs 3.17 lakh crore — numbers that mark a dramatic transformation in how India's poorest citizens access the formal financial system.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who launched the scheme on August 28, 2014, described its impact as "unparalleled" in a social media post marking the anniversary. The Finance Ministry said the average deposit per account now stands at Rs 5,356, a 3.4-fold increase over the program's lifetime.

From 35% to 89% Bank Ownership

The scale of the shift is visible in independent data. According to the World Bank's Global Findex 2025, 89% of Indian adults held a bank account in 2024, up from just 35.2% in 2011 and 53.1% in 2014 when the scheme launched. India's Financial Inclusion Index has risen from 53.9 in 2018 to 67 in 2026.

About 78% of PMJDY accounts have been opened in rural and semi-urban areas, reaching populations that had limited or no access to formal banking before 2014. Women hold approximately 56% of all accounts, reflecting the scheme's success in bringing crores of women into the financial mainstream.

Minister of State for Finance Pankaj Chaudhary highlighted the program's reach, noting that it has "empowered millions, particularly the marginalized sections, to access banking and financial services to improve their socio-economic conditions."

The JAM Trinity and Direct Transfers

Perhaps the most consequential impact of Jan Dhan accounts has been their role in the Jan-Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile (JAM) trinity, which the government uses to transfer welfare benefits directly to beneficiaries' bank accounts. More than Rs 53 lakh crore has been transferred through this system, eliminating intermediaries and reducing leakage in subsidy delivery.

"What began with the simple but profound objective of giving every citizen access to a bank account has evolved into an ecosystem of savings, social security, digital payments and formal credit."

— Binod Kumar, MD & CEO, Indian Bank

Account holders receive free RuPay debit cards — 41.29 crore have been issued — with accident insurance cover of up to Rs 2 lakh. Eligible holders can also access an overdraft facility of up to Rs 10,000, providing a formal credit lifeline for those previously dependent on informal lenders.

Building a Financial Ecosystem

The scheme has served as a foundation for several linked programs. Enrolments under the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (life insurance) stand at 27.84 crore, while the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (accident insurance) has reached 58.78 crore enrollees. The Atal Pension Yojana has enrolled 9.29 crore beneficiaries as of June 2026.

Jan Dhan accounts also helped India's digital payments ecosystem scale rapidly. The infrastructure of hundreds of millions of bank accounts provided the base on which the Unified Payments Interface was built, enabling simple, instant digital transactions across the country.

What Lies Ahead

The Finance Ministry has signaled that the next phase of financial inclusion will focus on deepening usage rather than expanding access. Technologies including the Unified Lending Interface, Account Aggregator framework, and Banking BHASHINI — which addresses language barriers in digital banking — are being deployed to transform Jan Dhan accounts from basic savings instruments into gateways for credit, insurance, and investment.

For India's diaspora, the scheme has practical implications: family members who previously lacked formal bank accounts can now receive remittances directly, access micro-insurance, and participate in government benefit programs without intermediaries.
nri_angle: Jan Dhan accounts enable NRIs to send remittances directly to family members in rural India who previously lacked formal banking access, while the JAM trinity ensures welfare benefits reach intended recipients.
